newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Tough NZ mkt depresses CDL Hotels profit.
newsitem.headline: Tough NZ mkt depresses CDL Hotels profit.

text.p: CDL Hotels New Zealand Ltd said on Friday that a 26 percent decline in year net profit to NZ$15.47 million refected competitive trading conditions caused by significant new hotel inventory emerging in various key New Zealand cities.

"While long term growth prospects for the tourism sector both in Australia and New Zealand continue to be positive, New Zealand will continue to experience competitive trading conditions in the next few years," CDL said in a statement.
CDL said that as the 2000 Olympics drew closer, the Sydney hotel market would continue to strengthen, which augured well for the group.
Several major new initiatives had been put in place and some important new strategic alliances had been concluded.

"Hotel management is confident of maintaining and slowly increasing its market share. The positive prospects of the subsidiaries' New Zealand land development and Australian property development activities will cushion the impact of the competitive New Zealand hotel environment in the next few years," CDL said. -- Wellington Newsroom (64 4) 4734746
